meta.source: Muse artifact the-crowd-live, via published actions only (getToday/startPlay/submitGuess/submitText/getContribute/getStats)
meta.note: 2026-11-16 full research audit: every stored answer now traces to a real published statistic (survey, census, government stat, or peer-reviewed figure) with a per-question source field. Questions with no real stat were removed, not estimated. Text lists are full 32-answer ranked lists. Player voting is a gimmick only — stored researched answers are authoritative and never flip to vote %. See VERIFICATION.md for the audit table.
meta.knownGap: 19 questions from the live Muse artifact (139 rows) were never harvested into this repo and remain unrecovered (suspected ids 7, 15, 21, 23, 26, 27, 36, 57, 58, 61, 74, 139, 146 + 6 unknown; id 13 deliberately excluded). A subagent harvest attempt on 2026-11-16 was blocked — no access to the artifact's published actions from a subagent session. This bank now holds 142 questions (119 audited - 10 removed + 33 new researched), so it exceeds the artifact's count, but those 19 artifact questions are still missing. Add them only via the artifact's published actions + fresh real-statistic research; do not invent values.

audit.standard: Real published statistic or remove — no soft estimates.

questions.text: What % of people think pineapple belongs on pizza?
questions.source: YouGov Oct 2025 poll of 1,126 US adults: 48% like or love pineapple on pizza, 44% dislike or hate it.

questions.text: What % of people have pretended to be on the phone to avoid talking to someone?
questions.source: Pew Internet & American Life Project 2011 survey of 2,277 US adults: 13% of cell owners had pretended to be using their phone to avoid interaction.

questions.text: What % of people check their phone within five minutes of waking up?
questions.source: Asurion 2022 survey of ~2,000 US adults: 75% check their phone within 5 minutes of waking up.

questions.text: What % of people have fallen asleep during a movie at the theater?
questions.source: YouGov Oct 2024 poll of 1,134 US adults: 39% have fallen asleep during a movie in a theater.

questions.text: What % of pet owners talk to their pets like they're people?
questions.source: Preply survey of 1,500 American pet owners, July 2023: 84% regularly talk to their pets like fellow humans

questions.text: What % of people have Googled their own name?
questions.source: Pew Research Center survey, Apr-May 2013: 56% of internet users have used a search engine to look up their own name.

questions.text: What % of Americans pick cold pizza over standard breakfast foods?
questions.source: Slice survey of Americans (reported via Delish/Mashed): 53% pick cold pizza for breakfast over standard breakfast foods.

questions.text: What % of people keep a junk drawer they couldn't fully explain?
questions.source: Junk King 2024 survey: 95% of Americans admit to having at least one junk drawer in their home.

questions.text: What % of people have sent a text to the wrong person?
questions.source: Sky Mobile survey of 2,000 UK adults, Apr 2025: 61% have sent a text to the wrong person.

questions.text: What % of people believe they've seen a ghost?
questions.source: YouGov, Oct 2025: 16% of US adult citizens reported having seen a spirit or ghost

questions.text: What % of people sing in the shower?
questions.source: Mira Showers / YouGov survey of 2,061 UK adults, Apr 2018: 1 in 10 people sing in the shower.

questions.text: What % of people have lied about having seen a famous movie?
questions.source: MSC Cruises UK study of 2,000 Brits, 2017: 40% had claimed to have seen a film they have never seen.

questions.text: What % of people would eat food that fell on the floor — five-second rule?
questions.source: Bosch survey of 2,000 UK adults, Mar 2025: 73% would eat food that had fallen on the floor if retrieved quickly.

questions.text: What % of people set multiple alarms to wake up?
questions.source: University of Notre Dame snoozing study (450 professionals, 10 months): 57% were habitual snoozers, defined as using multiple alarms to wake.

questions.text: What % of people haven't killed a houseplant in the last two years?
questions.source: Blooming Artificial survey of 1,000+ UK adults, 2024: 40% had not killed a houseplant in the last two years.

questions.text: What % of people read the terms and conditions before clicking agree?
questions.source: Deloitte Global Mobile Consumer Survey 2017, 2,000 US adults: 9% read terms and conditions in full before agreeing (91% accept without reading).

questions.text: What % of people think they're a better driver than average?
questions.source: YouGov Daily Question, 6 Sep 2018 (UK adults)

questions.text: What % of people couldn't recall a friend's phone number without looking it up?
questions.source: Kaspersky Lab digital amnesia study, 2015, 1,000+ US adults: 51.4% were unable to call their friends without looking up the number.

questions.text: What % of Facebook users would give up Facebook for a month for $500?
questions.source: Allcott, Braghieri, Eichmeyer & Gentzkow, American Economic Review 2020 (NBER WP 25514, 2,743 US Facebook users): almost 20% had willingness-to-accept over $500 to deactivate for four weeks, median $100.

questions.text: What % of millennials have a 'chair' covered in clothes right now?
questions.source: Unilever market research, 2018 (reported by Reuters): 60% of millennials have a 'chairdrobe'.

questions.text: What % of people talk to themselves out loud when alone?
questions.source: WebMD citing a study of adults: 25% of adults talk to themselves out loud.

questions.text: What % of people quit their New Year's resolution by the end of January?
questions.source: Forbes Health/OnePoll survey, 2024 (n=1,000 US adults)

questions.text: What % of people prefer the window seat on a plane?
questions.source: PhotoAid survey of 1,095 US adults, Dec 2024: 58% prefer window seats.

questions.text: What % of people have rewatched an entire TV series from start to finish?
questions.source: Brightcove / OnePoll poll of 2,000 UK adults, Jul 2018: 45% had rewatched an entire series from start to finish.

questions.text: What % of Brits think they could qualify for the 2028 Olympics if they started training today?
questions.source: YouGov, August 2024 (n=2,070 GB adults)

questions.text: What % of people have snooped through a partner's phone at least once?
questions.source: Pew Research Center survey of ~5,000 US adults: 34% of people in relationships have snooped on their partner's phone without permission.

questions.text: What % of people eat the crust on their pizza?
questions.source: YouGov pizza poll, Apr 11-13 2023, 1,000 US adults: 79% typically eat the crust of their pizza.

questions.text: What % of people have bought something just because it was on sale?
questions.votePrompt: Have you ever bought something just because it was on sale?
questions.source: Capital One Shopping impulse-buying data, 2025: 70% of consumers have impulsively bought an item because it was on sale.

questions.text: What % of everyone alive today lives in Brazil?
questions.note: About 216 million Brazilians out of roughly 8.1 billion people on Earth.
questions.source: UN World Population Prospects 2024 (Worldometer): Brazil = 2.60% of world population in 2024

questions.text: What % of US adults hold a PhD?
questions.note: Doctorates are rare everywhere.
questions.source: US Census Bureau, American Community Survey 2022: ~2% of US adults hold a doctoral degree

questions.text: What % of US households own a boat?
questions.source: National Marine Manufacturers Association / US Coast Guard: 11.9% of US households own a recreational boat

questions.text: What % of people are both left-handed AND red-haired?
questions.note: Left-handed is about 10% and red hair about 2% — both at once barely registers.
questions.source: Computed: ~10% left-handed (de Kovel et al. 2019) x ~2% red-haired = 0.2%

questions.text: What % of Iceland's population was not born in Iceland?
questions.source: UN / World Bank data via GeoRank: 25.1% of Iceland's population was not native-born (2024)

questions.text: Ice cream showdown — how does the crowd split?
questions.source: YouGov, America's favorite ice-cream flavors, July 2022 (head-to-head: vanilla 49%, chocolate 43%)

questions.text: US pet dogs and cats — what's the split?
questions.source: AVMA Pet Ownership and Demographics Sourcebook / Pet Owner Survey 2025: 87.3M dogs, 76.3M cats

questions.text: Sleep schedules — how do people split?
questions.source: YouGov, 'Are you more of an early bird or a night owl?', May 27 2022

questions.text: Phones in the US — how do owners split?
questions.note: Apple holds a slim US majority; worldwide this split flips the other way.
questions.source: StatCounter Global Stats, US mobile OS market share 2025: iOS 58.21%, Android 41.52%

questions.text: Where Americans actually live — how does the population split?
questions.source: U.S. Census Bureau, 2020 Census urban/rural classification (released Dec 29, 2022): 80.0% urban, 20.0% rural

questions.text: US college students — what's the gender split?
questions.note: Women have been the majority on US campuses for decades.
questions.source: NCES Digest of Education Statistics, Table 306.10, fall 2023 enrollment

questions.text: US nurses — what's the gender split?
questions.note: One of the most lopsided job splits there is.
questions.source: Data USA, Registered nurses workforce profile 2024 (ACS): 87.8% women

questions.text: Breakfast table — how does the crowd split?
questions.note: Savory wins the morning.
questions.source: Parade / SheKnows, What America Eats survey, April 2013: 73% prefer savory breakfast

questions.text: Vacation vote — how does the crowd split?
questions.note: Sand beats altitude by a comfortable margin.
questions.source: Travel Channel / Open Mind Strategy, Summer Travel Forecast 2019: 63% beach over mountains

questions.text: Morning fuel — how does the crowd split?
questions.note: Coffee runs the morning.
questions.source: CivicScience, Coffee or Tea polling, Jan 2024-Jul 2025: coffee 65%, tea 35%

questions.text: US paid workdays — how do they split?
questions.source: Barrero, Bloom & Davis, Survey of Working Arrangements and Attitudes (WFH Research), June 2026: ~27% of paid workdays from home

questions.text: What % of women over 50 will break a bone because of osteoporosis?
questions.source: International Osteoporosis Foundation survey via UCB (2024): almost one in two women after age 50 experienced a fracture

questions.text: What % of people have a third nipple?
questions.note: Published estimates are all over the place — medical reviews report anywhere from 0.2% to 5.6% of the general population. This question uses the low end: 0.2%, about 1 in 500 people. Source: Polythelia: A Case Report, Annals of Obstetrics and Gynecology (2024).
questions.source: Polythelia case report, Annals of Obstetrics and Gynecology (2024): supernumerary-nipple prevalence 0.2%-5.6%

questions.text: What % of adults still sleep with a stuffed animal?
questions.source: Build-A-Bear / Atomik Research survey of 2,000 adults: 40% sleep with a stuffed animal (reported by CNN, 2025)

questions.text: What % of adults are still a little afraid of the dark?
questions.source: Talker Research, Sept 2025 (n=2,000 US adults): 29% still afraid of the dark

questions.text: What % of people have sleepwalked at least once?
questions.source: Stallman & Kohler (2016), PLOS ONE: lifetime prevalence of sleepwalking 6.9%

questions.text: What % of people bite their nails?
questions.source: Halteh et al. (2017): onychophagia affects approximately 20-30% of the general population

questions.text: What % of people keep a secret snack stash nobody else knows about?
questions.source: Popchips / Talker Research, May 2026 (n=5,000 US adults): 60% keep secret snack stashes at home

questions.text: What % of Americans keep cash at home as part of their savings?
questions.source: LendingTree / DepositAccounts survey, Feb 2026 (n=2,000 US consumers): 27% keep cash at home as savings

questions.text: What % of Americans have never left their home state?
questions.source: OnePoll / Victorinox survey of 2,000 Americans: 11% have never travelled outside their birth state

questions.text: What % of people think they could survive a week alone in the wilderness?
questions.source: YouGov 'Confidence in Capabilities' poll, June 18-22, 2026 (n=1,109 US adult citizens)

questions.text: What % of car owners have given their car a name?
questions.source: Talker Research / Ziebart survey of 2,000 US car owners, Jun 2025: 21% have bestowed their car with a name.

questions.text: What % of people have fallen asleep on a bus or train and missed their stop?
questions.source: Vodafone / Bryter survey of 2,103 UK residents, Sep 2015: 30% have missed their stop on public transport; one in three have slept through their stop.

questions.text: What % of everyone who has ever been to space flew as a private citizen?
questions.source: Space Daily, June 2026: ~120 private civilians of ~700 total people who have ever been to space = ~17%

questions.text: What % of people were born on February 29th?
questions.note: Leap day comes once every four years — roughly 1 birthday in 1,461.
questions.source: Calendar math: 1 in 1,461 days is February 29 = 0.068%

questions.text: What % of people have perfect pitch?
questions.note: About 1 person in 10,000 can name a note with no reference.
questions.source: Frontiers in Neuroscience (2016): absolute pitch prevalence in Western populations estimated 0.01%-0.07%; Ward (1999): 1 in 10,000

questions.text: What % of US households own a business jet?
questions.source: Computed: 26,670 business jets/turboprops on FAA register (Oct 2026) / 132.7M US households (Census ACS 2024) = 0.02%

questions.text: Ketchup storage — how do households split?
questions.note: The fridge crowd wins big — the pantry loyalists hold their ground anyway.
questions.source: Heinz UK, 'Where do you keep yours?' poll, June 2023: 63% fridge, 37% cupboard

questions.text: Toilet paper — how does the crowd hang it?
questions.note: Over wins — and the original patent drawing agrees.
questions.source: Cottonelle/Kimberly-Clark Roll Poll, March 2010: 72% over, 28% under

questions.text: The story was better as a…?
questions.note: The book usually wins this argument.
questions.source: ThriftBooks / OnePoll, Books on the Big Screen survey, Dec 2021: 67% prefer the book

questions.text: Reaching out — how do people split?
questions.source: Pew Research Center, Americans and Text Messaging, Sept 2011: 31% prefer text, 53% prefer voice call

questions.text: Shower timing — how do people split?
questions.source: The Harris Poll, Shower Habits: What Americans Really Do, Feb 2024: 60% morning, 33% night

questions.text: Driving on a warm day — how do people split?
questions.note: AC wins the highway; windows down owns the back roads.
questions.source: Hankook Tire Gauge Index, via US Daily Review: AC 61%, open windows 39%

questions.text: US households — what's the own/rent split?
questions.note: About two in three US households own their home.
questions.source: U.S. Census Bureau, Quarterly Residential Vacancies and Homeownership, Q2 2026: homeownership rate 65.0%

questions.text: What's the first thing most people do when they wake up?
questions.source: PrepScholar Family Feud questions: 'What's something you do when you wake up in the morning?' — Check your phone 27, Hit snooze 20, Go to the bathroom 15, Eat breakfast 12, Get dressed 11 (survey format, n=100 per question). Corroborated by the game's own guess bank id 3 (84% check phone within 5 minutes of waking).

questions.text: Name the most common thing people forget at home
questions.source: Shane Co. survey of 2,000+ people across 44 states (2023): phones were the most commonly misplaced item in almost every state; keys (41%) and wallets (40%) close behind. GoCountry 105 community poll (Feb 2026), 'What item is most forgotten when leaving the house?': cell phone confirmed by the page admin as the #1 answer, ahead of wallets, sunglasses, keys.

questions.text: What's the most popular pizza topping?
questions.source: YouGov US survey of 1,000 adults, Apr 2023 (reported The Focus, 9 Feb 2024): favourite topping Pepperoni 24%, Sausage 13%, Extra cheese 11%, Mushrooms 9%, Chicken 6%, Pineapple 4%, Bacon 4%, Peppers 4%, Meatballs 3%, then Onions/Salami/Olives/Fresh tomato/Ham/Fresh garlic/Fresh basil/Jalapeños at 2% each; anchovies least favourite (29% say no).

questions.text: Name the excuse people give most for being late to work

texts: The dog wouldn't let me leave

unlisted: my horoscope told me not to go
a zebra was running down the highway
questions.source: CareerBuilder/Harris Poll survey (2014-2016 waves, 3,008 workers + 2,201 hiring managers): Traffic 39-51% #1, Oversleeping/lack of sleep 19-31% #2, Bad weather 7-28% #3, Too tired 23-25%, Forgetting something 13%, Public transport 8%, Dropping kids off 6-10%. Top-3 order stable across every wave.

questions.text: Name something most people have in their junk drawer
questions.source: Joybird survey of 1,900 Americans (2020): top-10 junk-drawer items in order — Tape 55.4%, Pens 54.8%, Spare batteries 53.1%, Scissors 50.7%, Flashlights 44.6%, Glue 43.6%, Paper clips 38.8%, Matches 37.0%, Rubber bands 36.0%, Keys 33.1%. Divert.co.uk poll of 1,800 (2023) also lists batteries first in the UK, confirming batteries is a top-3 answer either way.

questions.text: What's the most common fear people have?
questions.source: YouGov US poll (2014, 1,000 adults): snakes 64% at least a little afraid, heights 57%, spiders next; Gallup (2001, 1,016 adults): snakes 51% #1, heights 36%, public speaking 40% #2. Chapman Survey of American Fears Wave 9 (2023) confirms heights 33.2% 'afraid/very afraid' vs public speaking 28.7% and insects/spiders 25.3% among personal fears — but Chapman’s overall #1s are societal fears (corrupt government), so this prompt is framed as phobias, where snakes lead.

questions.text: Name the car most people dream of owning
questions.source: MoneySuperMarket global dream-car study (Dec 2025 data, 4,000-driver survey + 5-year Google search volume): Ford Mustang #1 worldwide with 116,686,707 searches; Porsche 911 #2, Dodge Charger #3, Tesla Model 3 #4, BMW M3 #5, Tesla Model Y #6. Tinting Chicago US survey (2,000+ Americans, 2024): Ford #1 overall dream-car brand, Toyota #2, Tesla #3. Family Feud board (2024, 'car men want but can't afford'): Lamborghini 25, Ferrari 14, Corvette 13, Porsche 10 — consistent tail, not top.

questions.text: Name the superpower most people say they'd want
questions.source: YouGov UK open-ended poll, 12-13 Mar 2025 (n=2,223 GB adults, free-text answers): Invisibility 19% #1, Ability to fly 15% #2, Teleportation 7% and Time travel 7% tied #3, Healing powers 6% #5, Reading minds 5%, Seeing the future 3%, Super strength 2%. NOTE: US closed-menu polls differ — YouGov US 2017 put Healing 37% #1; Marist US 2018 put Time travel 29% #1 — so the open-ended (free-choice) framing is the one used here.

questions.text: What's the most common first job people have?

texts: Working at an ice cream shop
Sales associate at a clothing store

unlisted: newspaper route as a formal job is now rare
questions.source: Moneypenny nationwide survey (published 28 Oct 2024, updated 2026): most common first jobs — Fast food 15% #1, Babysitting 12% #2, Retail 11% #3, Restaurant server 8% #4, Grocery store cashier 7% #5. BLS/CPS 2024 analysis (DesignRush, May 2025) corroborates the same cluster for 16-24s: cashiers 1.28m, waiters 877k, retail salespersons 739k, cooks ~600k.

questions.text: Name something people are always losing
questions.source: Shane Co. survey (2023, 2,000+ people, 44 states): phones the most commonly misplaced item in almost every state; keys 41% and wallets 40% close behind. Esure UK behavioural study (2,000+ participants): average person misplaces something 9x/day; top items Phone 45%, Keys 37%, Wallet/Cardholder 29%. Chipolo US/UK roundup: US top 5 are TV remote, phones, car & house keys, glasses, wallets; UK top 5 keys, phone, pens, glasses/sunglasses, remotes. Uber Lost & Found Index 2026: Phone #1 most forgotten in Ubers (1M+ reports), Wallet #2, Luggage #3, Keys #4.

questions.text: Name the place most people say they want to visit before they die
questions.source: British Airways poll of 2,000 UK residents (reported Stylist): top-30 'places to visit before you die' — #1 Eiffel Tower, Paris; Big Ben/London #3. Korean survey of 1,700 (age 13+): Paris 11% #1 dream destination, Sydney and New York 7% each. Budget Direct/Pureprofile survey of 1,002 Australians (Mar 2025): Tokyo 57% #1, Rome and London 47% tied #2, Paris 41% — Paris is top-4 in every national sample, #1 in the UK/Korean ones, which is the basis for keeping it.

questions.text: Name something in the kitchen most people never use
unlisted: a bread maker is not #1 — it is #8 in Direct Line
questions.source: Direct Line Home Insurance / Opinium survey, 4-7 Jan 2013, 2,013 UK adults: most commonly owned-but-unused kitchen gadgets — Toasted sandwich maker 26% #1, Food processor, Slow cooker, George Foreman grill, Blender, Kitchen scales, Juicer, Bread maker 16% #8, Hand blender, Coffee machine. HelloFresh study of 1,500 adults: bamboo steamers/tagines 53% never used, sushi mats 52%, spiralisers 52%, pasta makers 49% — corroborates the same single-purpose-appliance cluster.

questions.text: Name something people bring to a potluck
unlisted: salad was already unlisted in the bank — now rank 13
keys (was unlisted; not a food, excluded)
questions.source: Napa Cellars Friendsgiving survey (reported Sporked, Nov 2026): mac and cheese is the #1 most essential Friendsgiving side, ahead of mashed potatoes and stuffing. Campbell's State of the Sides Report 2026 (5,017 US adults, Reputation Leaders, Aug-Sep 2026): mac and cheese is Gen Z's #1 side for the second straight year, 57% say it is the dish everyone can agree on, 42% say there are never leftovers; overall Thanksgiving top 5 are Stuffing, Mashed potatoes, Sweet potatoes, Mac and cheese #4, Green bean casserole.

questions.text: Name something most people keep in their car's glove box
unlisted: the car title (advised against — theft risk)
a spare tire (does not fit in a glove box)
questions.source: Aviva survey of 4,000 nationally representative Brits aged 16+ (reported 2025, 'Miles of Memories'): top safety items in the glove box — Owner's manual and warranty information 42% #1, Phone chargers and tech gadgets 35% #2, First aid kit 29% #3, Car maintenance accessories like tyre pressure gauge 27% #4, Car registration and insurance documents 25% #5. Mechanic roundups (Morning Carpool, 2024) agree on the same document/tool cluster.

questions.text: Name a game almost everyone played as a kid

texts: What time is it Mr Wolf
Hide and seek in the dark

unlisted: monopoly (board game, not a playground game — excluded from this list; see new board-game prompt if wanted)
roblox (not a childhood game for most adults)
questions.source: Right to Play / Express survey of 2,000 adults (published 10 Jun 2025, for International Day of Play, 11 Jun 2025): Top 30 playground games of all time — #1 Hide and Seek, #2 Tag/You're It, #3 Skipping ropes, #4 Marbles, #5 Hopscotch, #6 Conkers, #7 British Bulldog, #8 What's the Time, Mr Wolf. A Family Feud-style recess board (2026) agrees on the same cluster: Tag, Hopscotch, Hide & Seek, Four Square, Kickball, Soccer.

questions.text: Name the first thing people buy when they move into a new place
questions.source: Mise En Casa new-home checklist (2026): 'Toilet paper is the most common miss... The couch can wait. Toilet paper can't.' HomeGuide first-home checklist (2026) agrees bed/sofa are first furniture, toilet paper and plunger top bathroom priorities.

questions.text: Name the most common tattoo people get
questions.source: Tatuantes (2025) citing global search data: butterfly is the most searched tattoo worldwide, then rose, dragon, flower, cross, lion, snake, wolf. Calendar-UK/SINGULART: butterflies most popular in the USA (201,000 monthly searches), rose 2nd (165,000), dragon 3rd (110,000).

questions.text: Name something people talk to even though it can't talk back
questions.source: OnePoll/TheJoyOfPlants survey of 2,000 UK adults (2021, via StudyFinds): over half chat with inanimate objects; 60% consider pet conversations two-way; 44% talk to plants; 24% shout at alarm clock; ~20% plead with their car; 10%+ thank an ATM. ReptileKnowledge survey: 83% of dog owners vs 68% of cat owners talk to their pet.

questions.text: Name something most people carry in their bag every day
questions.source: Art of the Bag 2026 Carry Report (2,000 US adults, Apr-May 2026): Phone 99%, Wallet/Cards 94%, Keys 91%, Lip balm 87%, Charger/Cable 82%, Hand sanitizer 79%, Snacks 67%.

questions.text: Name something most people have under their bed
questions.source: IKEA product-design insights via MetroReport (2026): seasonal linens are the most frequently stored under-bed item (74% of users); shoes, books and spare bedding are the standard under-bed categories. Bored Panda (Jan 2026, 1.6K comments) and My Tips Book threads: dust/dust bunnies, lost socks, shoes and pet hair dominate what people actually report under their beds.

questions.text: Name something that's always in the fridge door
questions.source: Ranker 'Best Condiments To Keep In The Fridge Door' (1,700+ voters, updated Oct 2025): current top 3 are Hot Sauce, Ketchup, Butter; FAQ lists the top 10 as Hot sauce, Ketchup, Butter, Salsa, Mustard, Mayonnaise, Barbecue sauce, Salad Dressing, Ranch, Soy sauce. Shelflife/Home of Innovation (2025): the fridge door is the correct home for condiments like ketchup, mustard, mayo, jams and hot sauces.

questions.text: Name the school subject most people say was their worst
questions.source: Gallup Youth Survey (2005, n=1,028 US teens 13-17): math is the most difficult subject for 37% (29% math generally + 6% algebra + 2% geometry), science 20%, English 18%, foreign languages/history/social studies each under 10%. EdWeek/Edutopia summaries agree: math ~37% dislike, science ~35%, foreign language ~25%, history ~20%.

questions.text: Name a smell most people love
questions.source: Harris-commissioned poll of 1,000 people (via Easier.com): #1 freshly baked bread, #2 bacon, #3 freshly cut grass, #4 coffee; rain, new books, petrol also listed. Air Wick survey of 2,000 Brits (via Paperblog): #1 sea breeze, #2 baking, #3 fish and chips, #4 cut grass, #5 coffee; vanilla #20, rain #35.

questions.text: Name a sound that wakes most people up at night
questions.source: MindLab/Lemsip sleep study (2009, via Medindia): women's top wake-up sounds are 1. baby crying, 2. dripping tap, 3. rowdiness, 4. snoring; men's are 1. car alarm, 2. howling wind, 3. buzzing fly, 4. snoring; a baby's cry woke the most men overall. Lemsip survey: weather (rain/wind/thunder) is the most commonly cited night noise (50%), 47% lose sleep to a snoring partner.

questions.text: Name something most people have in their pockets right now
questions.source: 2023 lifestyle survey of 2,500 adults (via Alibaba product-insights summary): Smartphone carried daily 98%, Keychain only 76%, Wallet 62%, Folded cash 41%, Coin purse 37%. Art of the Bag 2026 Carry Report (n=2,000): Phone 99%, Wallet/Cards 94%, Keys 91%.

questions.text: Name the household thing people break most often
questions.source: SquareTrade (via Android Authority): ~50 million cracked phone screens a year in the US alone - 5,761 an hour; 66% of consumers damaged a device in the past year. IAG/State Insurance NZ contents claims (2019-2021): mobile phones are the #1 claimed item (35,899 claims), then glasses (28,957), laptops (~20,000). NEISS study (2014-2023): drinking glasses cause one-third of household-glass injuries.

questions.text: Name the excuse kids give most for not doing their homework

texts: I had too much other homework
My mom forgot to wake me up
My mom didn't wake me up
I didn't know we had homework
I did it but forgot to turn it in
I did it, it's in my bag

questions.source: No ranked survey of homework excuses exists. Teacher-compiled lists (Jackson Public Schools guide and the standard '100 excuses' lists) consistently lead with: forgot the assignment, didn't understand it, lost/misplaced it, left it at home, dog ate it, was sick, printer broke. 'The dog ate it' is the iconic #1 answer in every published list and in Family Feud-style play.

questions.text: Name something most people pretend to like
questions.source: Mommy Poppins (2024, hundreds of reader responses to 'what are you convinced people are pretending to enjoy?'): kale was mentioned the most. BuzzFeed (2024) on the 24K-comment Reddit thread 'most overrated food you're convinced people are just pretending to enjoy': kale and wine are the top repeated answers. Upworthy/AskReddit (2025): top activities people pretend to like are LinkedIn, restaurant birthday songs, kids' birthday parties, work parties, wine tasting, social media, IPAs.

questions.text: Name something most people have on their keychain
questions.source: No ranked survey of keychain contents exists. EDC guides (PrimeSurvivor, Lemon8) list the standard keychain set: house and car keys first, then bottle opener, USB drive, flashlight, multitool, carabiner, charms. House keys are also the #1 most-forgotten item in the Dr. Farrah Gray poll thread, and the Art of the Bag 2026 report has keys in 91% of bags.

questions.text: Name something most people do in the car when they're alone

texts: Argue with someone in their head

questions.source: Pew Research Center (2006): 68% of US drivers sing out loud while driving, 58% talk on a handheld phone, 41% eat a meal, 38% shout/curse at other drivers, 16% groom. AA/Populus poll (21,408 UK drivers): sing 29-33% when alone, make plans 39%, lost in thought 23%, talk on phone 6%, pray 5%. YouGov/Vauxhall survey (10,000+ motorists): 9 in 10 sing, 69% talk to their car, 32% talk to themselves, 16% pick their nose. Youi Car Confessions (2025, n=2,020): 31% talk to themselves alone in the car, 38% of women have a cry in the car.

questions.text: What % of people pee in the shower?
questions.note: Nearly half of Americans admit to peeing in the shower at some point during the year — a quarter do it regularly.
questions.source: Talker Research survey of 2,000 US adults, Feb 2025: 45% pee in the shower at some point during the year, 24% regularly.

questions.text: What % of people use their phone on the toilet?
questions.note: Over two-thirds of Americans admit to scrolling on the toilet.
questions.source: Reviews.org 2026 Cell Phone Usage Stats, survey of ~1,000 US adults, Q4 2025: 67.9% use their phone on the toilet.

questions.text: What % of people fall asleep with the TV on?
questions.note: More than a third of Americans routinely drift off with the TV still on.
questions.source: Ohio State University Wexner Medical Center / Harris Poll, July 2022, 2,040 US adults: 37% fall asleep with the TV on.

questions.text: What % of people have a comfort show they rewatch when stressed?
questions.note: Nearly 9 in 10 Americans have a show they return to again and again when times get tough.
questions.source: CableTV.com survey of 1,000 Americans, 2023: 87% say they have a comfort show they turn to again and again.

questions.text: What % of people have texted someone in the same room as them?
questions.note: Most Americans have texted someone sitting in the very same room as them.
questions.source: Reviews.org 2026 Cell Phone Usage Stats, survey of ~1,000 US adults, Q4 2025: 60% have texted someone in the same room.

questions.text: What % of people sleep with their phone within arm's reach?
questions.note: Nearly three-quarters of people sleep with their phone within arm's reach.
questions.source: Asurion 2022 survey of ~2,000 US adults: 71% sleep with their phone within arm's reach.

questions.text: US public school teachers — what's the gender split?
questions.note: NCES National Teacher and Principal Survey 2020-21: about three-quarters of public K-12 teachers were female (77%).
questions.source: NCES, Characteristics of 2020-21 Public and Private K-12 School Teachers (NTPS), 2022

questions.text: Browsers in the US — how does traffic split?
questions.note: StatCounter full-year 2025 US share: Chrome 53.16%, Safari 29.8%; remaining share is Edge, Firefox and others, so 53 is Chrome's share of all US browsing, not a two-way total.
questions.source: StatCounter Global Stats 2025 (US, all platforms), via SQ Magazine

questions.text: Handedness — how does the world split?
questions.note: Papadatou-Pastou et al. 2020 meta-analysis in Psychological Bulletin, pooling 2.3M+ people: 10.6% left-handed, 89.4% right-handed.
questions.source: Papadatou-Pastou et al., Human handedness: A meta-analysis, Psychological Bulletin (2020)

questions.text: Babies born in the US — what's the split?
questions.note: CDC final 2024 birth data: sex ratio at birth 104.5 boys per 100 girls, i.e. about 51.1% of births are boys.
questions.source: CDC/NCHS, Births: Final Data for 2024, National Vital Statistics Reports Vol. 75 No. 2 (2026)

questions.text: Getting to work — how do US workers split?
questions.note: Census ACS 2024 Table B08301: 69.2% of US workers drove alone to work; the rest carpooled (9.2%), worked from home (13.3%), took transit (3.7%), walked or biked.
questions.source: U.S. Census Bureau, American Community Survey 2024, Table B08301

questions.text: US adults — smartphone or not?
questions.note: Pew Research Center Mobile Fact Sheet (2026): 91% of US adults own a smartphone, 98% own a cellphone of some kind; n=5,511, Jan-Jun 2026.
questions.source: Pew Research Center, Americans' Use of Mobile Devices in 2026 (Mobile Fact Sheet)

questions.text: The US population — what's the gender split?
questions.note: Census Bureau population estimates to July 2025: ~167.7M males vs ~174M females, i.e. 49% male / 51% female.
questions.source: U.S. Census Bureau, Annual Estimates of the Resident Population by Sex, April 2020-July 2025

questions.text: What's America's favorite ice cream flavor?
unlisted: vanilla is #1 in retail sales (Instacart/Circana) — preference polls and sales disagree, noted in source
questions.source: IDFA National Ice Cream & Frozen Novelty Trends Survey, Apr 2026 (Morning Consult, 2,205 US adults): Top 5 favourite flavours — 1. Chocolate (38% put it in top 5), 2. Butter Pecan (27%), 3. Vanilla (25%), 4. Cookies & Cream/Oreo (23%), 5. Caramel/Salted caramel (22%). Verasight (May 2026, n=1,000) found 50% name vanilla the most popular flavour — preference vs perceived-popularity split, flagged in unlisted note.

questions.text: Name the most common pet people have
unlisted: a Tamagotchi (a toy, not a pet)
questions.source: APPA 2025-2026 National Pet Owners Survey (reported 2025-2026): most popular pets by US households — Dog 69.8m households #1, Cat 49.2m #2, Fish 11.9m #3, Bird 6.9m #4, Small mammal 6.7m #5, Reptile 6.1m #6, Horse 3.5m #7, Guinea pig 2.4m, Hamster 2.3m, Turtle 1.9m. YouGov Jan 2025 (2,223 adults): 48% currently own a dog, 36% a cat — same top 2.

questions.text: What's the most popular Thanksgiving side dish?
questions.source: Campbell's State of the Sides Report 2026 (Reputation Leaders, Aug-Sep 2026, 5,017 US adults who celebrate Thanksgiving, 100/state): America's 5 favourite Thanksgiving sides — 1. Stuffing/dressing (favourite in 38 states), 2. Mashed potatoes, 3. Sweet potatoes, 4. Mac and cheese, 5. Green bean casserole. Mac and cheese is Gen Z's #1 side for the second straight year; 57% say it is the dish everyone can agree on.

questions.text: Name the most popular dog breed in America
questions.source: American Kennel Club registration statistics, 2025 rankings (released March 2026): French Bulldog #1 for the 4th straight year, Labrador Retriever #2, Golden Retriever #3, German Shepherd #4, Dachshund #5, Poodle #6, Beagle #7, Rottweiler #8, German Shorthaired Pointer #9, Bulldog #10. 2024 top 5 identical except Poodle #5.

questions.text: What's most people's favorite color?
questions.source: YouGov global color survey (2015, 10 countries on 4 continents): blue is the favorite color in every country surveyed (23-33% of respondents), 8-18 points ahead of second place; second is green, red or purple depending on the country. Joe Hallock's 2003 survey: 42% chose blue.
